context: Tests whether the agent checks .agents/rules/ for existing rules before writing a new naming rule, avoids duplicating already-covered conventions, writes a focused RULE.md that covers the gap, and produces a validation report that references the existing rules it found.

checklist.name: Found existing rules
checklist.description: validation-report.md explicitly names the existing rule found in .agents/rules/ (i.e., references 'typescript-interfaces' or its RULE.md)

checklist.name: No interface naming duplication
checklist.description: The new RULE.md does NOT re-state conventions about interface naming (no mention of `I` prefix, `IUser`-style, or interface vs. type choice) — these are already in the existing rule

checklist.name: No placement duplication
checklist.description: The new RULE.md does NOT re-state rules about placing interfaces in `src/types/` — this is already in the existing rule

checklist.name: Gap coverage
checklist.description: The new RULE.md addresses at least one naming concern not covered by the existing rule — such as file naming conventions (kebab-case vs. camelCase), function naming, or React component file naming

checklist.name: Lowercase-hyphenated directory
checklist.description: The new rule lives in a directory under .agents/rules/ with a lowercase hyphenated name (e.g., ts-file-naming, typescript-files, file-naming-conventions)

checklist.name: Specific conventions
checklist.description: Every convention in the new RULE.md names a concrete rule (e.g., 'Use kebab-case for all .ts files') — no vague statements like 'use consistent naming'

checklist.name: Directive form
checklist.description: Conventions use imperative directive form ('Use X', 'Name Y as Z') — not 'You should use X' or 'It is recommended'

checklist.name: No rationale in RULE.md
checklist.description: RULE.md does NOT include sentences explaining why conventions exist — only the conventions themselves

checklist.name: Under 100 lines
checklist.description: The new RULE.md has fewer than 100 lines total

checklist.name: Grouped by concern
checklist.description: The new RULE.md uses ## section headings to group related conventions (e.g., separate sections for file naming and function naming)
